nodes.summary: Let $p = (p_0, \dots, p_n)$ be a vector of natural numbers, regarding matrix $i$ (for $0 \le i < n$) as having $p_i$ rows and $p_{i+1}$ columns. The column count of a parenthesization of $n$ matrices with respect to $p$ is $p_{i+1}$ for a single leaf naming matrix $i$, and the column count of the right factor for a product node.
nodes.title: Column count of a parenthesization

nodes.summary: A matrix-chain cost is a pair of natural numbers counting the abstract events charged by matrix-chain ordering and reconstruction: the number of split candidates evaluated by the dynamic program, and the number of tree nodes emitted during reconstruction.
nodes.title: Matrix-chain cost

nodes.summary: Let $p = (p_0, \dots, p_n)$ be a vector of natural numbers, regarding matrix $i$ (for $0 \le i < n$) as having $p_i$ rows and $p_{i+1}$ columns. A parenthesization of $n$ matrices is dimension-compatible with $p$ when, at every product node, the column count of the left factor equals the row count of the right factor, where row and column counts are taken with respect to $p$. A single leaf is always…
nodes.title: Dimension-compatible parenthesization

nodes.summary: Let $p = (p_0, \dots, p_n)$ be a vector of natural numbers, regarding matrix $i$ (for $0 \le i < n$) as having $p_i$ rows and $p_{i+1}$ columns. A parenthesization of $n$ matrices is valid for $p$ when its leaf indices, read left to right, are exactly $0, 1, \dots, n - 1$, and it is dimension-compatible with $p$.
nodes.title: Valid parenthesization

nodes.summary: For every $n \ge 1$ and all natural numbers $p_0, \dots, p_n$, the matrix-chain ordering algorithm run on the dimensions $p_0, \dots, p_n$ evaluates exactly $\binom{n+1}{3}$ split candidates.
nodes.title: Split candidates evaluated by matrix-chain ordering

nodes.summary: For every $n \ge 1$ and all natural numbers $p_0, \dots, p_n$, the scalar-multiplication cost of the parenthesization returned by the matrix-chain ordering algorithm on the dimensions $p_0, \dots, p_n$ equals the optimal cost it reports.
nodes.title: Matrix-chain ordering reports the cost of its parenthesization

nodes.summary: For every $n \ge 1$, all natural numbers $p_0, \dots, p_n$ and every parenthesization $T$ of $n$ matrices that is valid for these dimensions, the optimal cost reported by the matrix-chain ordering algorithm on the dimensions $p_0, \dots, p_n$ is at most the scalar-multiplication cost of $T$.
nodes.title: Reported matrix-chain cost is a lower bound

nodes.summary: For every $n \ge 1$ and all natural numbers $p_0, \dots, p_n$, the parenthesization returned by the matrix-chain ordering algorithm on the dimensions $p_0, \dots, p_n$ is valid: its leaves are the matrices $0, 1, \dots, n - 1$ in order, each exactly once, and at every multiplication node the column count of the left factor equals the row count of the right factor, where matrix $i$ has $p_i$ rows and $p_{i+1}$…
nodes.title: Matrix-chain ordering returns a valid parenthesization

nodes.summary: For every $n \ge 1$ and all natural numbers $p_0, \dots, p_n$, the matrix-chain ordering algorithm run on the dimensions $p_0, \dots, p_n$ charges exactly $2n - 1$ reconstruction events.
nodes.title: Reconstruction size in matrix-chain ordering

nodes.summary: For every $n \ge 1$ and all natural numbers $p_0, \dots, p_n$, the total number of events charged by the matrix-chain ordering algorithm run on the dimensions $p_0, \dots, p_n$ is at most $3n^3$.
nodes.title: Cubic bound for matrix-chain ordering

nodes.summary: For every $n \ge 1$ and all natural numbers $p_0, \dots, p_n$, the total number of events charged by the matrix-chain ordering algorithm run on the dimensions $p_0, \dots, p_n$ is $\binom{n+1}{3} + (2n - 1)$.
nodes.title: Exact event count of matrix-chain ordering

nodes.summary: Given $n \ge 1$ and natural numbers $p_0, \dots, p_n$, where matrix $i$ of the chain ($0 \le i < n$) has $p_i$ rows and $p_{i+1}$ columns, the algorithm computes, bottom-up by interval length, values $m_{i,j}$ for $0 \le i \le j < n$: $m_{i,i} = 0$ and, for $i < j$, $m_{i,j}$ is the least value of $m_{i,k} + m_{k+1,j} + p_i p_{k+1} p_{j+1}$ over $i \le k < j$, and the first split point $k$ attaining it is recorded.…
nodes.title: Matrix-chain ordering

nodes.summary: The leaf indices of a parenthesization of $n$ matrices form the list of indices in $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ obtained by reading its leaves from left to right: $[i]$ for a single leaf naming matrix $i$, and the concatenation of the lists of the left and right factors for a product node.
nodes.title: Leaf indices of a parenthesization

nodes.summary: A parenthesization of $n$ matrices is a full binary tree whose leaves are labeled by indices in $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$: either a single leaf naming matrix $i$, or a product node with a left and a right parenthesization as factors. Labels may be repeated, omitted, or out of order.
nodes.title: Parenthesization

nodes.summary: A matrix-chain result for $n$ matrices pairs a natural number, the reported optimal scalar multiplication count, with a parenthesization of $n$ matrices, the reported optimal parenthesization. The structure itself does not require the count to be minimal or to be attained by the parenthesization.
nodes.title: Matrix-chain result

nodes.summary: Let $p = (p_0, \dots, p_n)$ be a vector of natural numbers, regarding matrix $i$ (for $0 \le i < n$) as having $p_i$ rows and $p_{i+1}$ columns. The row count of a parenthesization of $n$ matrices with respect to $p$ is $p_i$ for a single leaf naming matrix $i$, and the row count of the left factor for a product node.
nodes.title: Row count of a parenthesization

nodes.summary: Let $p = (p_0, \dots, p_n)$ be a vector of natural numbers, regarding matrix $i$ (for $0 \le i < n$) as having $p_i$ rows and $p_{i+1}$ columns, and let $r(T)$ and $c(T)$ be the row and column counts of a parenthesization $T$ with respect to $p$. The scalar multiplication count of a single leaf is $0$, and that of a product node with factors $L$ and $R$ is the sum of the counts of $L$ and $R$ plus $r(L)\,c(L)\,c(R)$.
nodes.title: Scalar multiplication count of a parenthesization

nodes.summary: The total of a matrix-chain cost is its number of candidate evaluations plus its number of reconstruction nodes.
nodes.title: Total matrix-chain cost

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
